title: How these physicists brought STEM to the doorstep of women, rural youth
syllabus: GS3 › Science and technology: awareness and popularisation · GS1 › Role of women · GS2 › Education; Role of NGOs
summary: Pune-based VigyanShaala International links rural youth and young women with STEM mentors and a free AI mentor on WhatsApp; over 20,000 young women in 28 states have joined its She for STEM programme.
ideas: Mentorship closes the access gap: curious students in remote areas often lack teachers who can answer them; sustained mentoring bridges that gap.
VigyanShaala shows that sustained mentorship can bring science to students whose schools cannot answer their questions.
Technology scales guidance: a free AI mentor on WhatsApp ('Curie') lets a student in a remote college ask a career question at midnight.
GS3 · AI for good / Digital education
AI tools like VigyanShaala's WhatsApp mentor 'Curie' can scale career guidance to remote students.
Women in STEM and first-generation learners: over 70% of the 20,000 young women in She for STEM are first-generation learners.
Over 70% of the 20,000 young women in She for STEM are first-generation learners, proof that mentoring widens women's access to science.
Civil society complements the state: a non-profit network of 1,000 mentors fills gaps in science education and career guidance.
Civil-society networks like VigyanShaala complement public science education with mentorship the state cannot provide alone.
